title: Rate-adaptive fleet safety net with predictive drop and soft fallback
creator: Aisha Patel
description: Build a fleet-level admission control safety net that adapts token admission and graceful degradation based on short-term arrival forecasts. Goal: guarantee minimum throughput for SLAs while avoiding catastrophic overload by combining predictive drop (forecast-driven early shedding), a soft fallback tier to compatible model variants or regional overflow, and coordinated burst token reservations with the autoscaler. This ticket covers design, prototype, and integration with routing, quota systems, and the Dedicated autoscaler. Success means demonstrable throughput guarantees under synthetic and real traffic spikes without violating per-customer SLOs and keeping error rates within thresholds.
acceptance_criteria: Prototype implements predictive arrival estimator (EWMA + short-window AR) and outputs an admission probability in the runtime path.
Fleet token-bucket controller enforces a configurable min-throughput reservation and a burst reservoir that can be consumed and replenished by the autoscaler flow.
Soft fallback routes accepted-but-shed requests to compatible lower-cost model variants or a regional overflow pool with documented latency/cost trade-offs.

End-to-end tests show at least 95% of SLA-class traffic maintains target throughput during 3x synthetic arrival bursts while tail latency degradation is bounded and error surface area is reduced compared to current behavior.
Dashboard panels (Grafana) added for forecasting signal, admission rate, reservoir level, and fallback ratio; alerts defined for reservoir exhaustion and forecast divergence.
design_decisions: Use a short-horizon EWMA + AR predictor rather than full ML forecasting to keep runtime overhead minimal and predictable.
Admission probability is calculated per-request at the fleet ingress layer; admitted requests consume from a fleet-level token reservoir to guarantee throughput across tenants.
Implement soft fallback using model variant mapping table (exact model -> compatible variants) rather than arbitrary rerouting to avoid semantic regressions.

Autoscaler integration exposes a 'burst_token_budget' metric and a REST hook for the autoscaler to prioritize capacity allocation when reservoir drains; this avoids tight coupling to autoscaler internals.
Keep per-customer guaranteed reservations orthogonal to fleet safety net; reservation slots cannot be preempted by safety net eviction to honor contractual commitments.

11/29: Integrated fallback-routing table; added simple latency and quality metadata to allow policy-driven fallback thresholds.
12/02: Coordinated with autoscaler team to add burst_token_budget metric (metrics PR: github.com/redwood-inference/autoscaler/pull/402).
Next: extend e2e load test, add chaos scenarios, and schedule design review with SRE and PM.
testing_plan: Unit tests for predictor correctness and admission probability bounds.
Integration tests: ingress -> admission -> token consumption -> fallback route executed in k8s canary cluster.
Load tests: replay production-shaped traces with synthetic 3x/5x bursts; assert min-throughput and tail-latency SLOs.
Chaos tests: simulate autoscaler delay, partial regional outage, and sudden reservoir exhaustion to verify graceful fallback behavior.
Canary rollout: 1% -> 5% -> 25% traffic with rollback guardrails tied to reservoir exhaustion alert.
risks_and_mitigation: Risk: Predictor false positives could shed healthy traffic — Mitigation: conservative smoothing, safety floor admission probability, and quick reversion on forecast divergence alerts.
Risk: Fallback model variants may regress quality — Mitigation: restrict fallback to vetted variants and attach quality metadata; track quality regressions with eval prompt set.

Risk: Autoscaler miscoordination leads to token starvation — Mitigation: autoscaler contract includes burst_token_budget SLA and emergency refill endpoint; add circuit-breaker between admission controller and autoscaler hook.
Risk: Increased operational complexity — Mitigation: provide a single-metric health indicator (safety_net_health) and clear runbook for SREs.
